title: Design a delivery workflow
description: A fictional example showing independent topics, nested conditions, prerequisites and source-aware decisions. Recommendations are examples, not approved policies.

nodes.title: Where does the workspace run?
nodes.prompt: Should the first release be local-first or depend on a hosted service?
nodes.example: A small team needs to review a decision document while travelling.

options.label: Local-first workspace
benefits: Works without a service account after the app is loaded.
risks: Backups and collaboration require explicit transfer.
options.example: A reviewer keeps a session locally and sends an export when ready.
options.outcome: A reviewer keeps a session locally and sends an export when ready.
options.rationale: Illustrative design trade-off for this sample. This is not a universal recommendation.

options.label: Hosted workspace
benefits: Shared access can be centrally managed.
risks: Authentication, operational ownership and data handling become release requirements.
options.example: Reviewers open a shared service, subject to access control.
options.outcome: Reviewers open a shared service, subject to access control.
options.rationale: Illustrative design trade-off for this sample. This is not a universal recommendation.

options.label: Leave this decision open
benefits: Avoid approving an unsupported policy.
risks: Dependent decisions remain unresolved.
options.example: This question stays deferred, not completed.

nodes.title: Local backup strategy
nodes.prompt: How should local work be backed up?
nodes.example: Browser storage may be cleared by the user or a device policy.

options.label: Explicit portable session export
benefits: The user controls when and where data leaves the browser.
risks: A user who never exports can lose their local workspace.
options.example: The reviewer downloads a session after completing a section.
options.outcome: The reviewer downloads a session after completing a section.
options.rationale: Illustrative design trade-off for this sample. This is not a universal recommendation.

options.label: Managed backup integration later
benefits: A future integration can automate a backup routine.
risks: That integration is not part of the first local release.
options.example: The first release documents the missing managed-backup feature.
options.outcome: The first release documents the missing managed-backup feature.
options.rationale: Illustrative design trade-off for this sample. This is not a universal recommendation.

options.label: Leave this decision open
benefits: Avoid approving an unsupported policy.
risks: Dependent decisions remain unresolved.
options.example: This question stays deferred, not completed.

nodes.title: Reminder placement
nodes.prompt: When should a local backup reminder be shown?
nodes.example: A reviewer has completed a whole topic since the last export.

options.label: After completing a topic
benefits: Prompts appear at a meaningful milestone.
risks: A long unfinished topic can still contain unsaved external backups.
options.example: A quiet reminder appears when a section is completed.
options.outcome: A quiet reminder appears when a section is completed.
options.rationale: Illustrative design trade-off for this sample. This is not a universal recommendation.

options.label: Only on explicit export actions
benefits: No interruptions during a review.
risks: The user must remember to make backups.
options.example: A persistent export button stays available.
options.outcome: A persistent export button stays available.
options.rationale: Illustrative design trade-off for this sample. This is not a universal recommendation.

options.label: Leave this decision open
benefits: Avoid approving an unsupported policy.
risks: Dependent decisions remain unresolved.
options.example: This question stays deferred, not completed.

nodes.title: Hosted access control
nodes.prompt: Which identity approach should a hosted release use?
nodes.example: Different teams should not see each other’s private sessions.

options.label: Team-managed accounts
benefits: Revocation and ownership are explicit.
risks: An identity and authorization implementation is required.
options.example: The release waits until tenant isolation and access tests pass.
options.outcome: The release waits until tenant isolation and access tests pass.
options.rationale: Illustrative design trade-off for this sample. This is not a universal recommendation.

options.label: Invite-only pilot
benefits: The initial audience can be constrained.
risks: Invites are not a substitute for authorization tests.
options.example: Only invited pilot accounts are provisioned.
options.outcome: Only invited pilot accounts are provisioned.
options.rationale: Illustrative design trade-off for this sample. This is not a universal recommendation.

options.label: Leave this decision open
benefits: Avoid approving an unsupported policy.
risks: Dependent decisions remain unresolved.
options.example: This question stays deferred, not completed.

nodes.title: Sample or sensitive content?
nodes.prompt: What content may the first demo include?
nodes.example: The demo will be shared with people outside the project team.

options.label: Fictional sample data only
benefits: The demo avoids exposing real decisions and notes.
risks: Users need to import their own document to evaluate a real use case.
options.example: Example company names and policies are fictional.
options.outcome: Example company names and policies are fictional.
options.rationale: Illustrative design trade-off for this sample. This is not a universal recommendation.

options.label: Reviewed real data
benefits: The example is closer to a real workflow.
risks: Content owners must approve every shared fact and note.
options.example: The demo waits for a documented content review.
options.outcome: The demo waits for a documented content review.
options.rationale: Illustrative design trade-off for this sample. This is not a universal recommendation.

options.label: Leave this decision open
benefits: Avoid approving an unsupported policy.
risks: Dependent decisions remain unresolved.
options.example: This question stays deferred, not completed.

nodes.title: Real-data release review
nodes.prompt: Who approves real content before it enters a shared demo?
nodes.example: A source document may contain internal comments or personal names.

options.label: A named content owner
benefits: One responsible reviewer can approve the release scope.
risks: A named owner still needs a clear review checklist.
options.example: The owner signs off on the exact exported document.
options.outcome: The owner signs off on the exact exported document.
options.rationale: Illustrative design trade-off for this sample. This is not a universal recommendation.

options.label: Two reviewers
benefits: Independent review may catch missed details.
risks: Review requires more coordination.
options.example: Two reviewers compare the same content snapshot.
options.outcome: Two reviewers compare the same content snapshot.
options.rationale: Illustrative design trade-off for this sample. This is not a universal recommendation.

options.label: Leave this decision open
benefits: Avoid approving an unsupported policy.
risks: Dependent decisions remain unresolved.

nodes.title: Local session retention
nodes.prompt: Who controls when local sessions are removed?
nodes.example: A reviewer wants to keep several projects but clear one completed session.

options.label: Explicit user reset with confirmation
benefits: The action has a clear scope and can be preceded by an export.
risks: The user must manage old sessions.
options.example: Reset clears the selected session while other projects remain.
options.outcome: Reset clears the selected session while other projects remain.
options.rationale: Illustrative design trade-off for this sample. This is not a universal recommendation.

options.label: Design a retention policy before release
benefits: A policy can define a consistent retention period.
risks: Expiry behaviour needs consent, communication and tests.
options.example: Automatic expiry is left out until its policy is approved.
options.outcome: Automatic expiry is left out until its policy is approved.
options.rationale: Illustrative design trade-off for this sample. This is not a universal recommendation.

options.label: Leave this decision open
benefits: Avoid approving an unsupported policy.
risks: Dependent decisions remain unresolved.
options.example: This question stays deferred, not completed.

nodes.title: Release evidence
nodes.prompt: What evidence is needed before sharing the pilot?
nodes.example: Automated tests pass but no keyboard or touch review has happened.

options.label: Automated gates plus manual review
benefits: Rendering and input issues can be checked separately from engine correctness.
risks: Manual review takes time and requires real environments.
options.example: The release report distinguishes test results from browser and device checks.
options.outcome: The release report distinguishes test results from browser and device checks.
options.rationale: Illustrative design trade-off for this sample. This is not a universal recommendation.

options.label: Explicitly limited technical preview
benefits: Feedback can start with accurately stated limitations.
risks: It must not be presented as a production-ready release.
options.example: The README labels it an early preview and lists missing checks.
options.outcome: The README labels it an early preview and lists missing checks.
options.rationale: Illustrative design trade-off for this sample. This is not a universal recommendation.

nodes.title: Pilot rollout
nodes.prompt: Should the pilot be opened to a small group first?
nodes.example: A team wants feedback before inviting a broader audience.

options.label: Small pilot first
benefits: Feedback can be acted on before broader distribution.
risks: Pilot success does not prove behaviour at every scale.
options.example: Five reviewers test the documented workflows before a wider invitation.
options.outcome: Five reviewers test the documented workflows before a wider invitation.
options.rationale: Illustrative design trade-off for this sample. This is not a universal recommendation.

options.label: Open preview with clear boundaries
benefits: More people can try the tool.
risks: Incoming feedback can be harder to prioritize.
options.example: A public preview lists supported and unsupported workflows.
options.outcome: A public preview lists supported and unsupported workflows.
options.rationale: Illustrative design trade-off for this sample. This is not a universal recommendation.

options.label: Leave this decision open

nodes.title: Hosted pilot check
nodes.prompt: How will the hosted pilot establish its operational owner?
nodes.example: A hosted pilot needs someone to review access and incidents.

options.label: Name an owner and review date
benefits: Ownership remains visible.
risks: The owner needs time and access to the necessary evidence.
options.example: The pilot record names the owner and the next review date.
options.outcome: The pilot record names the owner and the next review date.
options.rationale: Illustrative design trade-off for this sample. This is not a universal recommendation.

options.label: Hold the hosted pilot until ownership exists
benefits: No unattended hosted service is implied.
risks: The hosted route remains deferred operationally.
options.example: The team continues with the local demo while hosting is planned.
options.outcome: The team continues with the local demo while hosting is planned.
options.rationale: Illustrative design trade-off for this sample. This is not a universal recommendation.

nodes.title: Feedback channel
nodes.example: A report should include the document shape and expected decision status.

options.label: Repository issues with a minimal example
benefits: Reports can be linked to tests and fixes.
risks: Private documents must be removed from public reports.
options.example: A contributor attaches a fictional minimal document.
options.outcome: A contributor attaches a fictional minimal document.

options.label: An internal review queue
benefits: Private feedback can stay inside a team.
risks: External contributors cannot follow the same queue.
options.example: The team summarizes confirmed issues into a sanitized tracker.
